column3: The Hebrew repeats the image “advanced in days”; BSB expresses this idiom as “well along in years”.
The Hebrew uses the collective singular “the Geshurite”; BSB uses the plural.
The Hebrew says the Shihor is “before Egypt”; BSB specifies “east of Egypt”.
The Hebrew joins Mearah with “and”; BSB introduces it with “from”. “The Canaanite” and “the Amorite” are collective singulars.
The Hebrew uses the collective singular “the Gebalite” and says “toward the rising of the sun”; BSB uses a plural and “to the east”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins “with it/him” and explicitly names the Reubenite and Gadite in collective singulars. BSB supplies “the other half of Manasseh” and uses plurals.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the collective singular “the Amorite” and calls the Ammonites “the sons of Ammon”.
The Hebrew uses collective singulars for the Geshurite and Maacathite; BSB uses plurals.
Close to the Hebrew.
The two peoples are collective singulars joined with “and”; BSB uses plurals joined with “or” under the negation.
The Hebrew leaves the subject of “gave” implicit; BSB explicitly names Moses.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew places the plateau “at Medeba”; BSB says “beyond Medeba”.

The Hebrew uses “struck” rather than “killed” and calls Sihon king of “the Amorite”, a collective singular.

The Hebrew says “the Jordan and its border”; BSB condenses this to “the bank of the Jordan”.
The Hebrew names both “the tribe of Gad” and “the sons of Gad”; BSB condenses these.
The Hebrew calls the Ammonites “the sons of Ammon” and places Aroer “before Rabbah”; BSB says “near Rabbah”.
